title: Building Evy Energy
intro: Evy Energy was an EV charging software company that helped businesses connect and operate chargers, while giving drivers one app to find, access, and pay for charging. I co-founded it and led product design, product, and parts of engineering from 2022 until its acquisition by Zemetric in 2024.

sections.heading: Starting with charger discovery
body: Our first problem statement was simple: help EV drivers find a charger they could rely on. Existing listings were fragmented and often stale, so we assembled our own dataset from public information, driver groups, and site visits.

The directory answered where a charger was, not whether a driver could use it. Each network had its own driver app, payment system, and operating rules. Completing the journey required live availability, reservations, payments, and direct integrations with charging businesses.

sections.heading: What charging businesses needed
body: As we tried to onboard charging businesses as partners, they pushed us to solve the problem underneath the partnership: downtime. An offline charger meant a failed session and lost revenue, yet faults were often discovered only after a driver complained.
We needed connected chargers for the driver app. Charging businesses needed software infrastructure to keep those chargers online. The same system could solve both needs.

sections.heading: Building ChargeConnect
body: ChargeConnect was the charger-management platform. Its infrastructure layer exchanged data with connected chargers, while its web dashboard gave charging business teams one place to manage daily operations.
We built it closely with early charging businesses, turning recurring requirements into shared features instead of separate systems for every customer.

Chargers from different manufacturers did not always communicate or behave in the same way. We built the infrastructure layer of ChargeConnect to support multiple charger brands, so charging businesses could choose their hardware without changing their management platform.

sections.heading: Enabled charging session booking on driver app
body: Once charging businesses connected their chargers to ChargeConnect, the driver app no longer depended only on manually maintained listings. Drivers could now find a live charger, reserve it, start a session, pay, and track charging progress in one app.

sections.heading: Choosing how to scale Evy
body: By 2024, public charging was growing more slowly than we had expected, while white-label work was pulling us toward services. Scaling required larger customers and a stronger route through hardware, but becoming a hardware manufacturer was not what we wanted to build.
outro: Joining Zemetric placed ChargeConnect inside an established US charging company with its own hardware, access to new markets, and use cases across fleets, grids, and energy management. Zemetric acquired Evy Energy in April 2024.
